confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are bounded estimates from aggregator and cost-of-living pages. Several sources are undated or from 2025, and Argentine peso prices move quickly with inflation, so figures may already be stale. Beer and coffee are the better-supported anchors. Cocktail and wine-by-the-glass anchors are weak: no 2026 cocktail or glass-of-wine price was found, so cocktail is estimated from the Expatistan cocktail price relative to beer, and wine_glass is estimated from the beer price and a typical glass-to-beer ratio. Meal anchors use the range reported by several guides for a casual meal and a mid-range dinner for two without drinks. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of the city and were not checked against live listings. The FX observation (0.6720 USD per AUD, 18 Nov 2026) was taken from a secondary site (ozfinancehub.com.au) that reports RBA data. I did not open the rba.gov.au page itself, so it should be verified against the RBA F11 table.
comparable_city_reasoning: Basis is Buenos Aires-specific food and drink sources, cross-checked against each other. Accommodation tiers are benchmarked to general Latin American capital-city hotel and hostel levels, with Buenos Aires treated as a mid-to-upper Latin American capital for 3-star and as a moderately priced hostel market.
